g5ela-24-1-listen-words: This week's words are the ones a historian uses with care: claim, evidence, reasoning, treaty, removal, nation. Then formal style, the way an essay talks. In the game, peel the husks off a long word to find the base word inside.
g5ela-24-2-listen-words: Today, decide what each history word really claims. Then tell formal writing from casual talk, and sort long words by the part at their center. Three new ears of corn are waiting in the game.
g5ela-24-3-listen-words: Put the history words to work: primary source, secondary source, perspective, bias. Then practice naming your source before every claim. In the game, look for the part that can stand alone as a word.
g5ela-24-4-listen-words: One last time: say why the exact word matters when you write about history. Keep the novel and the record apart in every sentence. Then open the last three ears of corn.
